--- title: "[SurvivalBoost]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Gradient-boosted cumulative incidence model for competing risks. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_survival_boost.py#L106-L527){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python SurvivalBoost( *, n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=10, subsample=1.0, max_features=None, n_time_grid_steps=100, hard_zero_fraction=0.1, n_horizons_per_observation=3, epsilon_censoring=0.05, random_state=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Builds an ensemble of regression trees that estimates the cause-specific cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) and the any-event survival function via multi-class softmax gradient boosting. At each boosting iteration, random time horizons are sampled and concatenated as an extra input feature. IPCW weights correct for right censoring. The result is a flexible, nonparametric competing-risks model that learns CIFs directly from the data. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n_estimators]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of boosting iterations. Each iteration fits one tree per class (event type + survival). [learning_rate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.05]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Shrinkage applied to each tree's contribution. [max_depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum depth of each regression tree. [min_samples_leaf]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum number of samples required in each leaf. [subsample]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fraction of the training rows sampled (without replacement) per iteration. [max_features]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Features considered per split: `None` (all), `"sqrt"`, `"log2"`, an int, or a float. [n_time_grid_steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of time points in the default prediction grid. The grid is built from quantiles of observed event times. [hard_zero_fraction]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fraction of sampled time horizons forced to zero at each iteration, ensuring the model learns zero incidence at `t = 0`. [n_horizons_per_observation]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[3]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of independent time horizons sampled per subject at each iteration. Higher values give more stable gradients at the cost of larger per-iteration datasets. [epsilon_censoring]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.05]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Floor for censoring survival probabilities to prevent extreme IPCW weights. [random_state]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Seed or `numpy.random.Generator` for reproducibility. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit to synthetic competing-risks data and predict cumulative incidence: ::: {#e9b19571 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks(n=500, n_causes=2, n_covariates=3, seed=42) sb = gw.SurvivalBoost(n_estimators=50, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3, random_state=0) sb.fit(sim.surv, covariates=sim.covariates) sb ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` SurvivalBoost (50 rounds, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3) n = 500, events = 296, causes = 2, features = 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#1a5c1b20 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Predict survival and CIFs at specific times import numpy as np times = np.array([2.0, 5.0, 10.0]) cif = sb.predict_cumulative_incidence(sim.covariates, times=times) cif.shape # (n_subjects, n_events, n_times) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (500, 3, 3) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#dc451064 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Survival function surv = sb.predict_survival_function(sim.covariates, times=times) surv.shape # (n_subjects, n_times) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (500, 3) ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the gradient-boosted cumulative incidence model.
predict_cumulative_incidence() Predict cause-specific cumulative incidence functions.
predict_proba() Predict class probabilities at a single time horizon.
predict_survival_function() Predict the any-event survival function.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the gradient-boosted cumulative incidence model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_survival_boost.py#L227-L398){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, covariates=None, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A multi-state `Surv` response, built with `gw.Surv()` and a categorical `event`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `"Surv(time, factor(cause, c(0, 1, 2), c('censor', 'pcm', 'death'))) ~ age"` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe, a 2-D array, or a right-hand-side formula string evaluated against `data`. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `covariates`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [self]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator. ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a boosted CIF model to synthetic competing-risks data and inspect the result. The model learns a separate tree per class at each round: ::: {#7797527e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw sim = gw.simulate_competing_risks( n=500, n_causes=2, n_covariates=3, seed=42 ) sb = gw.SurvivalBoost( n_estimators=50, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3, random_state=0 ).fit(sim.surv, covariates=sim.covariates) sb ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` SurvivalBoost (50 rounds, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3) n = 500, events = 296, causes = 2, features = 3 ``` ::: ::: ### [predict_cumulative_incidence()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict cause-specific cumulative incidence functions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_survival_boost.py#L400-L462){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_cumulative_incidence(newdata=None, *, times=None, format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates for prediction. A dataframe, 2-D array, or formula string. `None` is not supported (training covariates are not cached). A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Time points at which to evaluate the CIFs. Defaults to the training-time grid. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : When `None`, returns a 3-D NumPy array of shape `(n_subjects, n_events, n_times)`. Event index `0` is the survival probability (complement of all CIFs). Indices `1..K` correspond to cause-specific CIFs. When a DataFrame backend name is given (e.g., `"polars"`), returns a long-format table with columns `time`, `cause`, `subject`, and `probability`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray or DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A 3-D array or a long-format DataFrame. ::: ### [predict_proba()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict class probabilities at a single time horizon. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_survival_boost.py#L501-L527){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_proba(newdata, *, time_horizon) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns an array of shape `(n_subjects, n_classes)` where column 0 is the probability of remaining event-free and columns `1..K` are cause-specific CIFs at `time_horizon`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariates for prediction. A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [time_horizon]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The time at which to evaluate probabilities. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probabilities of shape `(n_subjects, n_classes)`. ::: ### [predict_survival_function()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict the any-event survival function. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_survival_boost.py#L464-L499){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict_survival_function(newdata=None, *, times=None, format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariates for prediction. A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Time points at which to evaluate. Defaults to the training-time grid. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : DataFrame backend for output. `None` returns a 2-D NumPy array of shape `(n_subjects, n_times)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray or DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Survival probabilities. :::
